structured_output.summary: Alabama does not tax the $18,708 of Social Security. It does tax federally tax-exempt interest unless the bonds were issued by Alabama or one of its local governments (§ 40-18-14; r. 810-3-14-.02). The prompt names no issuer and says to treat unlisted facts as false, so the $4,734 counts as Alabama income. Alabama taxable income is then $4,734 − $3,000 standard deduction − $1,500 personal exemption = $234, taxed at 2%, which gives $4.68. The engine took exactly these steps. It also assumed medical expenses of $2,584.80, apparently by adding Medicare Part B premiums the prompt never listed. That changes nothing, because itemizing (about $2,600) still comes out below the $3,000 standard deduction. Most of the models answering 0 assumed Alabama exempts all federally tax-exempt interest, which is wrong. Stage 1 stands. One of its sources, an Alabama Department of Revenue FAQ, actually covers the financial institution excise tax, but its conclusion rests on the statute and the regulation.
